title: The Love of Christ Compels Us
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Paul's Ministry
subpoints: The Corinthian church was divided and hostile to apostolic authority
Paul faced false accusations regarding his motives and integrity
Motivation is crucial for faithful service in the face of opposition

outline.title: The Source of Motivation: The Love of Christ
subpoints: The Greek genitive indicates Christ's love for us, not our love for Him
Christ's love is constant, infinite, and objectively satisfying
This love compels, controls, and impels believers to serve

outline.title: The Result: A New Creation
subpoints: Believers in Christ are new creations
Old ways of thinking and living have passed away
All things become new through the work of God

outline.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
subpoints: God reconciled the world to Himself through Jesus Christ
God did not impute the trespasses of the world to them
Believers are ambassadors for Christ, pleading on His behalf

outline.title: The Exchange: Sin and Righteousness
subpoints: Christ, who knew no sin, became sin for us
Believers become the righteousness of God in Him
This exchange is the basis for the call to be reconciled to God

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro continues the series on 2 Corinthians, focusing on the passage from chapter 5, verses 12 to 21. The message addresses the critical role of motivation in the Christian life, particularly when facing opposition, false accusations, or difficult circumstances. While Paul faced a hostile church in Corinth that questioned his integrity and motives, he found his drive not in human approval or personal feelings, but in the sovereign and unchanging love of Christ. The pastor emphasizes that this is not merely the believer's love for Christ, which can waver, but Christ's love for the believer, which is constant, infinite, and compelling. This divine love acts as the primary force that constrains and directs the believer's actions and service.

The sermon further explores the theological implications of this motivation, highlighting the concept of the "new creation." Those who are in Christ have experienced a fundamental transformation where old ways have passed away and all things have become new. This transformation is the result of God's initiative in reconciliation, where He reconciled the world to Himself through Jesus Christ, choosing not to impute their trespasses to them. Consequently, believers are entrusted with the ministry of reconciliation, serving as ambassadors for Christ who plead on His behalf for others to be reconciled to God.

The message concludes by examining the profound exchange described in verse 21, where God made Christ, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in Him. This objective work of Christ provides the secure foundation for the believer's motivation. It is the knowledge of this gospel, and the assurance of Christ's love and righteousness, that empowers believers to persevere in their calling, regardless of external resistance or internal struggle.
